notes: Performance page for a single-strategy dividend value SMA manager with two planted issues (C4 trough-dated cumulative headline, C6 unsubstantiated regional superlative) and two decoys (standard 1-, 5- and 10-year net and gross returns, and a fully disclosed third-party rating).

planted.span: Up 168.0% since the March 2020 market low. From the bottom of the pandemic sell-off on March 23, 2020 through June 30, 2026, our composite gained 168.0% cumulative, net of fees.
planted.explanation: The headline measures cumulative return from the exact market bottom, a start date chosen to maximize the result, which is not fair and balanced even though standard periods appear lower on the page.

planted.span: No dividend manager in Virginia can match our record of protecting client capital when markets fall.
planted.explanation: A comparative superlative about downside protection is stated as fact with no supporting data or source, and the page's own figures show the composite trailing its index over every standard period.

decoys.span: For periods ended June 30, 2026, the Dividend Value Equity composite returned 11.82% over one year, 9.40% a year over five years and 8.74% a year over ten years, net of fees (12.66%, 10.22% and 9.56% gross of fees).
decoys.why_ok: The composite's returns are given for the required 1-, 5- and 10-year periods ending at the most recent quarter-end, net of fees with gross no more prominent, and the table adds since-inception returns.

decoys.span: In May 2026, Kilnworth Fund Research assigned the Dividend Value Equity strategy a rating of four out of five stars in its Separately Managed Account Review. The rating reflects risk-adjusted returns, net of fees, for the three years ended March 31, 2026, measured against 212 U.S. large-cap value strategies. Welbourne Cadell did not pay to be considered for or to receive the rating; we pay Kilnworth an annual license fee of $3,500 to reference it in our marketing. A rating is not indicative of future performance, and other rating services may assess the strategy differently.
decoys.why_ok: The rating discloses its date, the rater's identity, the period of data it reflects (three years ended March 31, 2026) and that the firm paid no fee for the rating but pays a $3,500 annual license fee to use it.
